title: To amend the FISA Amendments Act of 2008 to extend the authorities of title VII of the Foreign Intelligence Surveillance Act of 1978 through April 30, 2026, and for other purposes.

claims.claim: Section 702 of the Foreign Intelligence Surveillance Act lets the NSA collect the communications of foreign targets
claims.sourceSpan: the Attorney General and the Director of National Intelligence may authorize jointly, for a period of up to 1 year from the effective date of the authorization, the targeting of persons reasonably believed to be located outside the United States to acquire foreign intelligence information
claims.note: Source attributes the authorization to 'the Attorney General and the Director of National Intelligence' acting jointly, carried out by elements of the intelligence community; the NSA is never named in the statute. Operationally conventional but extrinsic to the source text.

claims.claim: collect the communications of foreign targets
claims.sourceSpan: the targeting of persons reasonably believed to be located outside the United States to acquire foreign intelligence information

claims.claim: collect the communications of foreign targets without a warrant
claims.sourceSpan: Nothing in subchapter I shall be construed to require an application for a court order under such subchapter for an acquisition that is targeted in accordance with this section at a person reasonably believed to be located outside the United States
claims.note: No individual court order (warrant) required for acquisition targeting foreign persons.

claims.claim: when those targets contact Americans, those conversations are swept up too
claims.sourceSpan: communications of or concerning United States persons obtained through acquisitions authorized under subsection (a)
claims.note: Statute's own query definition acknowledges 702 acquisitions capture communications of or concerning U.S. persons (incidental collection).

claims.claim: The FBI can then search that database for information about U.S. persons without getting a separate warrant
claims.sourceSpan: Federal Bureau of Investigation personnel must obtain prior approval from a Federal Bureau of Investigation supervisor (or employee of equivalent or greater rank) or attorney who is authorized to access unminimized contents or noncontents obtained through acquisitions authorized under subsection (a) for any query of such unminimized contents or noncontents made using a United States person query term
claims.note: Source requires internal FBI supervisor/attorney approval (and written justification) for U.S. person queries, but imposes no court warrant — consistent with 'without a separate warrant.'

claims.claim: This bill extends that authority through April 30, 2026
claims.sourceSpan: effective April 30, 2026, title VII of the Foreign Intelligence Surveillance Act of 1978 (50 U.S.C. 1881 et seq.) is repealed.

claims.claim: with no new limits, oversight requirements, or reforms added
claims.sourceSpan: EXTENSION OF AUTHORITIES OF TITLE VII OF THE FOREIGN
claims.note: Absence-supported: the enacted text's only operative changes are the repeal-date substitutions (sec. 1(a)) and conforming cross-reference/heading edits to transition procedures (sec. 1(b)); no new minimization, oversight, or query limits appear.

claims.claim: Extends the NSA's authority to collect foreign targets' communications without a warrant
claims.sourceSpan: the Attorney General and the Director of National Intelligence may authorize jointly, for a period of up to 1 year from the effective date of the authorization, the targeting of persons reasonably believed to be located outside the United States to acquire foreign intelligence information
claims.note: NSA not named in source; authorization attributed to AG + DNI.

claims.claim: including Americans' conversations when they contact those targets
claims.sourceSpan: communications of or concerning United States persons obtained through acquisitions authorized under subsection (a)

claims.claim: through April 30, 2026, with no reforms attached
claims.sourceSpan: effective April 30, 2026, title VII of the Foreign Intelligence Surveillance Act of 1978 (50 U.S.C. 1881 et seq.) is repealed.

claims.claim: Allows the NSA to compel U.S. tech companies to hand over communications of designated foreign targets
claims.sourceSpan: the Attorney General and the Director of National Intelligence may direct, in writing, an electronic communication service provider to
claims.note: The directive/compulsion power is attributed by source to AG + DNI (with the AG filing enforcement petitions), not the NSA. 'U.S. tech companies' is a fair gloss for 'electronic communication service provider.'

claims.claim: compel U.S. tech companies to hand over communications of designated foreign targets without a warrant
claims.sourceSpan: immediately provide the Government with all information, facilities, or assistance necessary to accomplish the acquisition
claims.note: Compulsion confirmed by the enforcement provision authorizing a petition 'for an order to compel the electronic communication service provider to comply with the directive' (i)(5)(A); no warrant required (c)(4).

claims.claim: When those targets communicate with Americans, those conversations are collected — the FBI can then search that database for U.S. person data without a separate warrant
claims.sourceSpan: Federal Bureau of Investigation personnel must obtain prior approval from a Federal Bureau of Investigation supervisor (or employee of equivalent or greater rank) or attorney who is authorized to access unminimized contents or noncontents obtained through acquisitions authorized under subsection (a) for any query of such unminimized contents or noncontents made using a United States person query term
claims.note: Incidental collection per (f)(5)(B); FBI U.S. person query requires internal approval, not a warrant.

claims.claim: Extended through April 30, 2026 — no new limits or reforms
claims.sourceSpan: effective April 30, 2026, title VII of the Foreign Intelligence Surveillance Act of 1978 (50 U.S.C. 1881 et seq.) is repealed.

claims.claim: Introduced and signed into law in 48 hours
claims.sourceSpan: Apr. 16, considered and passed House.
claims.note: Source legislative history shows House passage Apr. 16, Senate passage Apr. 17, and 'Approved April 18, 2026' — a roughly 2-3 day sprint — but states no introduction date, so a precise '48 hours introduced-to-signed' figure is not anchored to source. Rapid passage itself is source-evident.

claims.claim: Title VII of FISA (Section 702) authorizes the NSA to surveil foreign targets abroad
claims.sourceSpan: the Attorney General and the Director of National Intelligence may authorize jointly, for a period of up to 1 year from the effective date of the authorization, the targeting of persons reasonably believed to be located outside the United States to acquire foreign intelligence information
claims.note: NSA not named in source; authorization attributed to AG + DNI.

claims.claim: surveil foreign targets abroad without a warrant
claims.sourceSpan: Nothing in subchapter I shall be construed to require an application for a court order under such subchapter for an acquisition that is targeted in accordance with this section at a person reasonably believed to be located outside the United States

claims.claim: This bill extends that authority through April 30, 2026 with no new conditions attached
claims.sourceSpan: effective April 30, 2026, title VII of the Foreign Intelligence Surveillance Act of 1978 (50 U.S.C. 1881 et seq.) is repealed.
claims.note: Extension supported; 'no new conditions' supported by absence in enacted text.

claims.claim: Amends Section 403(b)(1) of the FISA Amendments Act of 2008 (Public Law 110-261)
claims.sourceSpan:
Section 403(b) of the
FISA Amendments Act of 2008 (Public Law 110-261) is amended

claims.claim: to set a fixed April 30, 2026 repeal date for Title VII
claims.sourceSpan: effective April 30, 2026, title VII of the Foreign Intelligence Surveillance Act of 1978 (50 U.S.C. 1881 et seq.) is repealed.

claims.claim: tied to the enactment of the Reforming Intelligence and Securing America Act
claims.sourceSpan:
the date of enactment of the Reforming Intelligence and
 Securing America Act

claims.claim: replacing a rolling deadline
claims.sourceSpan: two years after
claims.note: The prior deadline was a fixed formula — 'effective two years after' the RISAA enactment date, i.e. a determinate calendar date (April 20, 2026) — not a rolling/floating one; 'rolling deadline' loosely mischaracterizes it.

claims.claim: The amendment takes effect on the earlier of the date of enactment or April 19, 2026
claims.sourceSpan:
The amendments made
by this section shall take effect on the earlier of the date of the
enactment of this Act or April 19, 2026.

claims.claim: No new minimization requirements, no new oversight mechanisms, and no restrictions on FBI queries of the collected data are included
claims.sourceSpan: EXTENSION OF AUTHORITIES OF TITLE VII OF THE FOREIGN
claims.note: Absence-supported; the enacted text only changes repeal dates and conforming cross-references.

claims.claim: extends Title VII surveillance authorities through April 30, 2026 but sets no reporting requirement on how those authorities are used during the extension period
claims.sourceSpan: effective April 30, 2026, title VII of the Foreign Intelligence Surveillance Act of 1978 (50 U.S.C. 1881 et seq.) is repealed.
claims.note: Extension supported; the bill itself adds no reporting requirement (absence).

claims.claim: sets a fixed April 30, 2026 expiration date but does not establish any conditions or framework governing further reauthorization after that date
claims.sourceSpan: effective April 30, 2026, title VII of the Foreign Intelligence Surveillance Act of 1978 (50 U.S.C. 1881 et seq.) is repealed.
claims.note: Fixed date supported; no reauthorization framework in enacted text (absence).

claims.claim: Section 403(b)(1) of the FISA Amendments Act of 2008 (Public Law 110-261) — Title VII repeal date changed from two years after enactment of the Reforming Intelligence and Securing America Act to April 30, 2026
claims.sourceSpan:
the date of enactment of the Reforming Intelligence and
 Securing America Act
claims.note: Direction confirmed: from a RISAA-enactment-tied deadline to a fixed April 30, 2026 (see paired span 'effective April 30, 2026 ... is repealed').

claims.claim: Signed into law by the President on April 18, 2026
claims.sourceSpan: Approved April 18, 2026.
claims.note: 'Approved' = presidential signature.

claims.claim: as Public Law 119-84
claims.sourceSpan: Public Law 119-84

claims.claim: Analysis omits the bill's Section 1(b) amendments to Section 404(b) of the FISA Amendments Act of 2008 (transition procedures / conforming cross-reference and heading edits).
claims.sourceSpan: Extension of Transition Procedures.--Section 404(b) of the FISA
claims.note: Technical/conforming provision with low lay-reader impact, but it is an operative part of the enacted text not surfaced anywhere in the analysis.

claims.claim: Analysis references only Section 403(b)(1); the parallel Section 1(a)(2) amendment to paragraph (2) (the 18 U.S.C. 2511 note) making the same April 30, 2026 date change is not separately noted.
claims.sourceSpan: in paragraph (2) (18 U.S.C. 2511 note)
claims.note: Parallel date change to the companion note; minor.

notes: Reference-dependent bill: the enacted text (PL 119-84) only moves the Title VII repeal date to April 30, 2026 and makes conforming cross-reference edits; all substantive 'what Section 702 does' claims were judged against the registered referencedSource 50 U.S.C. 1881a (2024 edition). No material errors. Recurring minor flag: the analysis names 'the NSA' as the collecting/compelling actor, but the statute attributes authorization and provider directives to the Attorney General and the Director of National Intelligence (collection carried out by unnamed elements of the intelligence community) — conventional but extrinsic to source. Stage/vote cross-check consistent: bill text 'Approved April 18, 2026' + 'Public Law 119-84' match stage=signed / likelihood=Enacted (note: bill-text legislative history dates House passage Apr. 16, whereas cache votes[] list Apr. 17 — structured-field discrepancy, not a prose claim).
